events.headline: Houthi Missile Strike on Yemen Training Camp Death Toll Revised Up to 73, Deadliest of War's New Phase
events.summary: The toll from the October 19 Houthi ballistic missile strike on the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre in Shabwa, Yemen was revised upward to 73 killed, with over 200 wounded and 14 missing. Victims were mostly recruits aged 18-20 for a new 'Rapid Intervention' force; it is the deadliest single strike since Yemen's civil war resumed roughly three months ago.

events.headline: Brazil's Runoff Polls Close With Lula-Bolsonaro Race Still Too Close to Call
events.summary: Polls closed at 5pm Brasília time on Oct 25 in Brazil's presidential runoff between Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. No winner has been confirmed in available reporting, with the race described as razor-thin. Results are expected to be announced later in the evening.

events.headline: Trump Says US 'Could Strike Iran Tomorrow' as CENTCOM Preps Expanded Target List
events.summary: On Oct 24-25, Trump said the US 'could strike Iran tomorrow' or reach a deal, calling for a permanent end to Iran's nuclear program. CENTCOM has prepared an expanded strike-option target list for Defense Secretary Hegseth, while a DNI memo warning of 'advanced' Iranian plots against US officials abroad prompted reduced staffing at embassies in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE.

events.headline: Saudi Arabia Postpones Flagship FII Investment Conference to 2027 Citing Security Situation
events.summary: Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26-29, to 2027, citing the security situation following Houthi missile attacks including the Riyadh airport strike. The airport has remained closed; scheduled speakers included Jamie Dimon, Jane Fraser, David Solomon and Larry Fink.

events.headline: UN Says 1,123 Killed in Haiti Gang Violence Over Three Months, Security Forces Tied to Over Half of Casualties
events.summary: A UN Security Council briefing on Oct 19 reported 1,123 people killed and 440 injured in Haiti gang violence from mid-July to mid-October, with gang members responsible for 659 deaths. Security-force operations were linked to 52% of those killed or wounded. Gangs have adapted tactics in Saint-Michel-de-l'Atalaye, Marigot and Léogâne, while elections remain on hold.

events.headline: Putin Agrees to Resume Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks, Releases Detained American
events.summary: Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, during which Russia released American Stephen Hubbard, detained since 2022. A US official said Russia and Ukraine agreed to resume trilateral technical peace talks after November 10.

events.headline: Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Kills at Least 16 in Tibet's Baqen County
events.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu, Tibet, at 22:33 local time on October 22, killing at least 16 people and injuring over 50. The quake collapsed more than 339 homes, prompting deployment of over 1,600 rescuers.

events.headline: UN Says Drone Strikes Killed at Least 306 Across Sudan in First Three Weeks of October
events.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said drone strikes killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds across Sudan in the first three weeks of October, attributing attacks to both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the RSF. Strikes hit homes, markets, hospitals and infrastructure in Kordofan, Darfur, Blue Nile and Khartoum, encompassing the earlier Abyei market strike toll.

events.headline: DRC's Kabila-M23 FRN Coalition Names Leaders as Fighting Spreads to Uvira, South Kivu
events.summary: The Kabila-aligned FRN coalition with M23 named its leadership, including Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga as vice presidents. Fighting has spread from Walungu into the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira district of South Kivu, with government-coalition forces reportedly losing positions in the Bijombo highlands after drone strikes, materializing earlier warnings of a 'general attack.'

events.headline: Attacks on Shipping in Strait of Hormuz Surge to Wartime High
events.summary: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high in October, with about 27 attacks recorded this month according to IMO figures. Oil flow through the strait has fallen to roughly 68% of its pre-war baseline, about 11.6 million barrels per day versus 17.1 million.

events.headline: UN Warns Taiz, Yemen Could Run Out of Wheat Within Weeks as Houthi Siege Tightens
events.summary: The UN warns that wheat and flour supplies in Taiz could run out within three weeks after Houthi forces tightened their blockade by seizing the city's last main road link to other areas. Food prices have risen about 50%, more than 600,000 people including 200,000+ children depend on aid, and medical supplies are nearing depletion.

events.headline: US 'Southern Spear' Strikes on Drug Boats Have Killed at Least 238 Since Campaign Began
events.summary: US military strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific have killed at least 238 people across more than 79 strikes as of early October, part of the Trump administration's 'Southern Spear' campaign. A strike on Oct 4 killed 4 more. Human rights groups have called the strikes possible extrajudicial killings.

events.headline: Islamic State-Linked Fighters Kill at Least 48 Civilians Near Menaka, Eastern Mali
events.summary: On October 18, fighters from the Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP) raided Idaksahak pastoralist communities near Menaka, killing at least 48 civilians. The attack was reportedly carried out in retaliation for suspected informants aiding a Malian army drone strike.

events.headline: Nigeria Confirms Bundibugyo Ebola Strain Matches DRC Outbreak, 44 Contacts Monitored
events.summary: Nigerian health officials confirmed on Oct 20 that the imported Ebola case matches the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain from the DRC outbreak that began in May 2026, marking the first spread of that outbreak to West Africa. Forty-four contacts have been identified and are under monitoring.

events.headline: France Deploys 70,000 Police, Shuts Louvre and Metro Stations Ahead of Nationwide Protests
events.summary: Ahead of Oct 24 nationwide protests, France deployed about 70,000 police and gendarmes, closed the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais, shut over 24 Metro stations, and banned demonstrations in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier while allowing restricted marches in Paris and Marseille. The measures follow rioting and looting on Oct 17 that led to roughly 2,700 detentions.

events.headline: Hurricane Vance Holds at Category 2 South of Puerto Vallarta, Landfall Possible Oct 26-27
events.summary: Hurricane Vance remained a Category 2 storm with about 110mph winds roughly 365 miles south-southwest of Acapulco as of Oct 24, moving slowly north-northwest. Forecasters say it could make landfall near Puerto Vallarta, Mexico on Oct 26-27, or it could remain offshore.

events.headline: 150,000 Rally in Belgrade in Final Push Before Serbia's Oct. 25 Election
events.summary: Around 150,000 people rallied in Belgrade on October 21-22, the final demonstration by the student-backed opposition before Sunday's election. Civil society groups warned the election environment falls short of free-and-fair standards.

events.headline: US Ambassador Pledges Up to $20 Billion in Financing for Argentina Tied to Milei's Policies
events.summary: US Ambassador Peter Lamelas said on Oct 21 that US financing agencies could mobilize up to $20 billion in investment and financing for Argentine infrastructure, energy and mining projects through the end of 2027 — nearly three times a prior $7 billion commitment. The pledge is explicitly tied to Argentina maintaining President Milei's economic policies through the 2027 election, amid an ongoing bond selloff.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill More Palestinians in Gaza as Death Toll Since Ceasefire Nears 1,500
events.summary: On October 22, Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza City, Khan Younis, and near Jabalia. Health officials say roughly 1,500 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, while Israel reports four soldiers killed in the same period.

events.headline: South Korea Says North Korea Has Planted Nearly One Million Landmines Along DMZ Since 2024
events.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff told parliament on Oct 23 that North Korea has planted approximately 960,000 landmines along the DMZ since April 2024. The disclosure follows North Korea's Oct 21 order for border troops to take 'prompt and resolute action,' with Kim Yo Jong confirming new 'firepower units' are in position.

events.headline: Israel-Lebanon Talks in Tampa End Without Deal as Israeli Strikes Intensify in South Lebanon
events.summary: Two days of US-mediated Israel-Lebanon military talks at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa ended on October 22 without a breakthrough on Hezbollah disarmament verification. Israeli strikes and demolitions escalated in south Lebanon, hitting Kfar Tebnit and other villages.

events.headline: CENTCOM Marks 100 Days of Naval Blockade on Iran as IRGC Maintains Hormuz Closure
events.summary: US CENTCOM marked 100 days of its naval blockade of Iranian ports on October 22, saying it has blocked roughly $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. Iran's IRGC had earlier declared the Strait of Hormuz closed "until US conditions are met" and warned of strikes on US-escorted vessels.

events.headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv With Three Waves of Ballistic Missiles Hours After Witkoff-Putin Meeting
events.summary: Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles plus drones at Kyiv overnight on October 21-22 in three waves, killing one person and injuring up to 24. The attack damaged an ambulance station, a monastery, and metro bridge infrastructure, coming hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg.

events.headline: Student Protests Spread Across Indonesia as Worst Regional Haze in a Decade Persists
events.summary: More than 500 protesters gathered outside the Central Kalimantan governor's office on Oct 23 demanding a national haze emergency declaration. Indonesia's health ministry reports over 333,000 acute respiratory illness cases across seven provinces since mid-August amid Southeast Asia's worst haze in a decade.

events.headline: Hundreds of Thousands Join Coordinated Cost-of-Living Protests Across France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania
events.summary: Simultaneous demonstrations swept Europe on Oct 24: France saw 410,000-800,000 protesters and about 1,000 arrests; Italy saw protests in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna and Florence with 371 briefly detained; Spain's Madrid saw pension protests; Portugal saw housing-crisis demonstrations; and Albania saw anti-government protests. Clashes with police involved tear gas and water cannons in several cities.

events.headline: Italy Deploys Extra Troops to Milan as Cost-of-Living Protests Turn Violent in Several Cities
events.summary: During nationwide protests on Oct 24, Italian police briefly detained 371 people and arrested 9 after stones, bottles and firecrackers were thrown in Turin, Bologna and Florence. The Meloni government deployed 500 additional soldiers to Milan and condemned the violence while protests also occurred in Rome.

events.headline: Israel Locks Down West Bank After Hebron Checkpoint Attack Kills Two Soldiers
events.summary: Two Palestinian gunmen attacked a checkpoint near Hebron on Oct 23, killing Israeli soldiers Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, and wounding three others before being killed themselves. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered Hebron sealed and a full West Bank closure, calling for an intensified military campaign.

events.headline: Russian Strikes Kill Four Across Ukraine as Kyiv Sanctions 51 Russians Over Missile Production
events.summary: Russian strikes on Oct 24 killed 4 and injured 78 across Ukraine using 126 drones and 61 jet-powered missiles, hitting a residential building in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district. Ukraine struck back at the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant and a warehouse in Siberia roughly 2,500km from the border, and hit a Belgorod shopping complex, killing one. Zelensky separately sanctioned 51 Russian citizens and 44 entities tied to Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101 and Kinzhal missile component production.

events.headline: Albania Protesters Set Fire to Agriculture Ministry Door in Tirana Clashes, 300+ Injured
events.summary: Protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama over corruption, education and the cost of living, ongoing since mid-October, escalated on Oct 24 when demonstrators set fire to the agriculture ministry's door in Tirana. Police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets, and more than 300 protesters and police officers were injured while government buildings, banks and shops were damaged.

events.headline: Venezuela Government and Opposition Agree to Review Laws Barring Opposition Candidates
events.summary: In a third round of talks at Miraflores Palace on Oct 22, Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez met opposition negotiator Dinorah Figuera and Jorge Rodríguez. The sides committed to review laws used to disqualify opposition politicians, including the Organic Comptroller Law and an anti-terrorism financing law, and discussed parity in a delegation on Bank of England-held gold. A fourth round of talks is set for Nov 11-15.

events.headline: Ethiopia Names Interim Tigray Administration as It Accuses Eritrea of 60km Incursion
events.summary: Ethiopian PM Abiy Ahmed announced a six-month interim administration for Tigray on Oct 16, appointing five officials including a Mekelle mayor and pledging future elections. Separately, Ethiopia told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops advanced up to 60km into Tigray between Sept 29 and Oct 6; Eritrea denies invading and calls Ethiopian counter-threats a 'declaration of war.'

events.headline: Rubio Urges Cubans to Secretly Work With CIA as Trump Floats Sending Him to Negotiate
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Oct 23 urged Cubans seeking political change to discreetly partner with the CIA, while President Trump said Washington would 'take care of Cuba' and might send Rubio to finalize a deal. Cuban officials condemned the remarks as the CIA posted Spanish-language instructions for contacting the agency.

events.headline: Bangladesh Dengue Deaths Rise to 376 as Measles Toll Tops 1,200
events.summary: Bangladesh's dengue death toll reached 376 as of Oct 24-25, up from 357, with 1,898 new hospitalizations reported. The combined confirmed and suspected measles death toll reached 1,214 as of Oct 23, including 104 confirmed deaths and 1,110 suspected.

events.headline: Houthi Ballistic Missiles Aimed Near Mecca, Medina and Jeddah Intercepted, Saudi Flights Suspended
events.summary: Saudi coalition forces intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Mecca and Medina regions and Riyadh on Oct 24-25, with debris falling in Wadi Al-Maghmmas, Jeddah's Al-Nuzha district, Wadi Jalil near Taif, and the Rabigh resort area. Flights to Riyadh and Dammam were suspended through Nov 7 and to Jeddah through Oct 31. The Houthis denied targeting holy cities, saying they struck oil and military infrastructure.

events.headline: Thousands of Venezuelans Join First Nationwide Opposition Protest in Nearly Two Years
events.summary: Thousands demonstrated nationwide on October 22 in the first country-wide opposition protest in nearly two years, organized by Maria Corina Machado's Vente Venezuela. Protesters demanded a 2027 election date, Machado's return, and the release of political prisoners.

events.headline: Spain's Valencia Region Continues Flood Recovery After Storm Adam Killed Up to Five
events.summary: Storm Adam, a DANA weather system, brought up to 720mm of rain to Spain's Valencia and Alicante regions from Oct 17-20, killing 4-5 people and triggering confinement orders in 145 municipalities with over 1,000 emergency rescues. Prime Minister Sánchez visited affected areas and offered compensation of up to €6,000 per household as recovery continued into Oct 24-25.

events.headline: Pakistan Army Says Five Soldiers, 25 Militants Killed in Kurram Border Clashes as Talks Continue
events.summary: Pakistan's military said five soldiers and 25 Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan militants were killed overnight into Oct 25 in clashes as militants attempted to cross into Kurram and North Waziristan from Afghanistan. The fighting occurred even as Pakistani and Afghan Taliban delegations met in Istanbul the same day for Qatar- and Turkey-mediated ceasefire talks.

events.headline: Eight Inmates Killed in Simultaneous Ecuador Prison Riots as Opposition Candidate Jailed
events.summary: Near-simultaneous riots on Oct 22 at Cotopaxi No. 1 prison in Latacunga and El Inca prison in Quito killed eight inmates and injured about ten. Separately, a judge ordered pretrial detention for leftist presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez in a $500,000 money-laundering case tied to her 2023 campaign; any link between the two events is unconfirmed.

events.headline: Ecuadorian Presidential Candidate Luisa González Ordered Into Pre-Trial Detention Over Money Laundering
events.summary: A judge in Riobamba ordered pre-trial detention on Oct 24 for Ecuadorian presidential candidate Luisa González and two co-defendants in the 'Laberinto' case, involving roughly $500,000 in alleged money laundering tied to her 2023 campaign financing. González was transferred to a prison in Riobamba, Chimborazo province.

events.headline: Pakistan, Turkey, Qatar, Indonesia Sign 'Badr' Defense Cooperation Pact in Doha
events.summary: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia signed the "Badr" memorandum of understanding in Doha on October 21, deepening defense-industry cooperation. The pact includes provisions for joint production and technology transfers among the four nations.

events.headline: PAHO Maintains Highest Alert Level as Americas Report 1.69 Million Dengue Cases, Rising Chikungunya
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization continues its highest Grade-3 response to multi-country dengue and chikungunya outbreaks. As of mid-September, the Americas recorded 1.69 million suspected dengue cases (3,413 severe, 571 deaths), a 58% year-on-year decrease overall but rising in Andean, Central American and Caribbean countries. Some 213,919 suspected chikungunya cases were reported across 20 countries, including renewed transmission in Guyana.

events.headline: 18-Floor Unfinished Building Collapses in Nairobi, Several Missing
events.summary: An 18-floor unfinished building with occupied ground-floor and basement shops collapsed on 9th Street in Nairobi's Eastleigh area on Oct 23. Seven people were reported missing or trapped, one woman was rescued alive, and 66 of 67 construction workers escaped. Kenya Red Cross, the military and county emergency teams are responding; the building had no occupation certificate.

events.headline: Libya's Eastern Parliament Ratifies Turkey Maritime Deal, Egypt and Greece Reject It
events.summary: Libya's eastern, Haftar-aligned House of Representatives ratified a 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum on Oct 20-21, reviving a dispute with Egypt, Greece and Cyprus over eastern Mediterranean rights. Greece called it a breach of international law, Egypt declared it null and void, and Turkey's foreign minister said conditions were 'ripe' for Libyan east-west reunification.

events.headline: Armed Men Storm Libya's National Audit Bureau to Install Rival Deputy Head
events.summary: Masked armed men stormed the Tripoli headquarters of Libya's National Audit Bureau on Oct 21 to forcibly install Anwar al-Housh as deputy head under an appointment by the High Council of State. The Bureau suspended all operations in response. The move was condemned by UNSMIL, the United States and the United Kingdom.

events.headline: China's Economy Grows 4.5% in Q3, Beating Forecasts
events.summary: China's National Bureau of Statistics reported Q3 GDP growth of 4.5% year-on-year, up from 4.3% in Q2, beating forecasts, with cumulative growth of 4.6% for the first three quarters of 2026. Growth was driven by exports and high-tech manufacturing despite sluggish domestic consumption.

events.headline: Ukraine Confirms Starshield Speeds Restored After SpaceX Lifted Two-Week Slowdown
events.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry confirmed on Oct 24 that Starshield internet speeds have been restored above 400km/h after SpaceX had capped them at 160km/h since Oct 14. Musk said the restriction stemmed from a terms-of-service violation that has now been closed. Zelensky thanked partners for resolving the issue, which had disrupted Ukrainian drone operations.

events.headline: France Confirms World's First Known Human Case of Shamonda Virus, Patient Died
events.summary: France has confirmed the world's first known human case of Shamonda virus, a midge-borne livestock virus, in a severely immunocompromised patient treated at Hospices Civils de Lyon who has since died. Health authorities identified a new 'Shamonda-Europe' strain but say there is no broader public health risk.

events.headline: Fire Destroys Hitler-Era 'Eagle's Nest' Retreat in Bavarian Alps, Suspect Detained
events.summary: A fire overnight on Oct 23-24 destroyed most of the Kehlsteinhaus ('Eagle's Nest'), a Hitler-era mountaintop retreat near Berchtesgaden, Germany. About 200 firefighters battled the blaze in snow and wind; no injuries were reported. A 33-year-old German suspect showing signs of mental illness was detained nearby and sent for psychiatric evaluation, with a possible political motive under investigation.

events.headline: Storms Austen and Boelo Cut Power to Hundreds of Thousands Across Western France, UK, Ireland
events.summary: Storm Austen, named Oct 20, cut power to about 300,000 homes in western France and 20,000 in southwest England. It was followed by Storm Boelo, which brought 70-80mph gusts to Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England, affecting the broader UK, Ireland and Benelux region through Oct 24.

events.headline: Italy's Truckers Ease Diesel-Price Protests After Government Approves Aid Decree
events.summary: Truckers and farmers who had blockaded Calabria's ports and airports since mid-October over diesel costs suspended their protests after Prime Minister Meloni's government approved a decree adding 106 million euros in tax credits plus farming and fishing aid. Drivers warned they could resume action if an Oct 27 meeting with Transport Minister Salvini fails.

events.headline: Portuguese Police Clear Housing-Crisis Protest Camps in Lisbon and Porto, Arrest 55
events.summary: Police cleared housing-crisis protest encampments in Lisbon's Rossio Square and in Porto on Oct 24-25, arresting 55 people. Protesters are demanding withdrawal of a bill that would ease evictions and end rent caps; thousands returned to the squares after the clearance.

events.headline: Argentine Judge Dismisses Fraud Probe Into Milei Over $LIBRA Meme-Coin Collapse
events.summary: Federal Judge Martinez De Giorgi dismissed the criminal fraud investigation into President Milei and his sister Karina over the February 2025 collapse of the $LIBRA memecoin, ruling the events did not constitute a criminal offense. A parallel probe into promoter Hayden Davis was also dismissed.

events.headline: China Shadows US Navy Ship Near Sabina Shoal in Philippines' Exclusive Economic Zone
events.summary: China's PLA Southern Theater Command accused the USS Charleston of 'illegally' entering waters near Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands, inside the Philippines' exclusive economic zone, on Oct 20, and said it dispatched naval forces to track the vessel. The US 7th Fleet said the transit was a routine, lawful operation.

events.headline: Thousands Protest Across Poland on Sixth Anniversary of Near-Total Abortion Ban
events.summary: Thousands marched in Warsaw and more than 20 other Polish cities on the sixth anniversary of the Constitutional Tribunal's near-total abortion ban under the slogan 'Red card for abortion.' The protests came days after parliament passed two liberalizing bills expected to face a presidential veto from Karol Nawrocki.

events.headline: Nigeria Evacuates 114 More Citizens From South Africa Amid Xenophobic Violence, Total Tops 2,100
events.summary: Nigeria evacuated 114 more citizens — 57 men, 23 women and 34 children — from South Africa on Oct 22 amid ongoing xenophobic and Afrophobic violence. It was the 16th such evacuation since June 10, 2026, bringing the cumulative total to 2,151 people evacuated.

events.headline: Three Hostages Held 10 Months in Central African Republic Freed, Flown to Bangui
events.summary: Three hostages — a sub-prefect and two elections authority staff — who were kidnapped in Bambouti on Dec 28, 2025, were released on Oct 19 after mediation brokered by the UN mission MINUSCA. They were flown to Bangui on Oct 22 and received by President Touadéra.

events.headline: India Issues Red Alert for Kerala Districts as Heavy Rain Raises Flood and Landslide Risk
events.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued red alerts for Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad districts on Oct 25, and for Idukki and Palakkad on Oct 26, warning of rainfall exceeding 204.4mm in 24 hours with flash flood and landslide risk. Schools were closed in the Oct 25 red-alert districts.

events.headline: Philippine Peso Hits 31st Record Low of 2026 at P63.615 per Dollar
events.summary: The Philippine peso closed at a fresh record low of 63.615 to the US dollar on Oct 23, its 31st record low this year. The decline was driven by elevated oil prices, September inflation of 7.2%, and broader dollar strength amid geopolitical tension.

events.headline: China Urges US to Halt Expansion of Outbound Investment Security Restrictions
events.summary: China's Commerce Ministry said on Oct 24 it urged the United States to halt proposed expansions of outbound-investment security restrictions covering biotech, high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing called the move discriminatory and reserved the right to take countermeasures.

events.headline: Explosion and Fire at Chemical Warehouse in León, Mexico Injures Several, Hundreds Evacuated
events.summary: A large explosion and fire broke out at a chemical warehouse in the San Nicolás area of León, Guanajuato, on Oct 23-24. Several people were injured and hundreds of residents were evacuated as a precaution. No confirmed death toll has been reported.

events.headline: IMF Raises Egypt's Growth Forecast to 5.1% but Flags Inflation and Currency Risks
events.summary: The IMF raised its forecast for Egypt's FY2025/26 GDP growth to 5.1%, up from 4.2% in April, citing resilient economic activity, remittances and tourism. The fund flagged risks from inflation, which stood at 14.5% in August, as well as currency pressure and elevated borrowing costs.

events.headline: Bay of Bengal Depression Forecast to Strengthen Into Cyclone, Threatening Andhra Pradesh Coast
events.summary: India's Meteorological Department said a low-pressure system in the Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression as of the night of Oct 24, centered near 15.5N, 91.0E. It is forecast to become a cyclonic storm by Oct 26 and reach the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coast around Oct 28. Sri Lanka is not expected to be directly hit but may see increased rain and wind.

events.headline: Colombia Extradites FARC-Dissident Front 33 Leader 'Mocho Olmedo' to United States
events.summary: Willington Henao Gutierrez, alias 'Mocho Olmedo' and second-in-command of the FARC-dissident Front 33, was extradited on Oct 23 to face US drug-trafficking and money-laundering charges in a Florida federal court. Six other Colombians were extradited in the same action.

events.headline: Senegal's 72-Hour General Strike Disrupts Healthcare, Schools, Transport Before Youth Olympics
events.summary: Senegal's Trade Union Front, representing 13 unions, led a 72-hour general strike from Oct 21-23 over wages, pensions and labor codes, disrupting hospitals, schools and Dakar's bus network, prompting a military deployment to maintain minimal transit service. The action came days before Dakar hosts the Youth Olympic Games opening Oct 31; the government called the strike unlawful.

events.headline: Historic Delhi Mosque Near PM Modi's Residence Served Six-Day Eviction Notice
events.summary: India's Land and Development Office declared the century-old, heritage-listed Race Course Mosque 'unauthorised' on Oct 19 and ordered it vacated within six days, after its electricity and water had been cut on Oct 7. The Delhi Waqf Board disputes the order, citing a 1977 gazette notification recognizing the site's Waqf status.

events.headline: Typhoon Rosal (Champi) Exits Philippine Area After Weakening, No Landfall
events.summary: Typhoon Rosal, known internationally as Champi — which earlier caused 527 injuries and mass power outages in Taiwan — exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on the morning of Oct 24 after weakening to 120km/h winds from a peak of 215km/h. The storm did not make landfall in the Philippines but brought moderate to heavy rain to Batanes.

events.headline: China Reports Two More Human H9N2 Avian Flu Cases in Children, Both Recovered
events.summary: China reported two additional human cases of H9N2 avian influenza in 1-year-old girls, one with poultry exposure in Henan and one linked to a live poultry market in Guangdong. Symptom onset was in late August and early September 2026, and both children recovered without hospitalization.

events.headline: Shooting Outside Memphis Event Center Wounds Five to Six, Suspect Arrested
events.summary: A fight outside an event center in the Oakhaven area of Memphis, Tennessee escalated into a shooting around 2am on Oct 24-25, wounding five to six people. Suspect Kendell Catron, 24, was arrested and charged with four counts of aggravated assault.
